title: Tier line rates ship as 67/100/267 Mbps, not the spec's 10/100/1000 Mbps ladder
detail: Spec unit model: "narrow = 10 Mbps (residential access) · standard = 100 Mbps (distribution) · wide = 1 Gbps (core)". Shipped ladder is 67/100/267 — a documented, mathematically forced deviation; the access/dist/core hierarchy the user asked for is not what ships.
recommended_fix: If the nominal ladder matters, rule on it explicitly (per-tier display canon as follow-up); otherwise accept and record the 67/100/267 ruling in the briefing as resolved.

title: Node health card % is still backlog ÷ one tick of capacity, not octet-counter utilization
evidence:
core/node_health.odin:87:
		pct = u32(units * 100 / u64(throughput))
app/render/node_health.odin:111-113:
	load_bytes := u64(units) * u64(pp.FRAME_BYTES) / u64(max(1, cat.balance.packet_bandwidth))
	node_rate := pp.format_rate(pp.line_rate_bps(u32(cat.balance.packet_bandwidth), throughput, cat.balance.logic_hz))
	trace := fmt.tprintf("%d%% (load %s / %s)", pct, pp.format_bytes(load_bytes), node_rate)
detail: Briefing: "utilization % from the new octet counters"; the bug = "the BACKLOG SNAPSHOT divided by ONE TICK of capacity". The node card's headline % is still stuck-packets×bw ÷ throughput (reads 150%), now dressed in bytes/rate.
recommended_fix: Derive the node card % from transmitted work (extend the tx ring to nodes), or relabel it as a backlog/oversubscription ratio rather than a bare percent.

title: Sim pipe warnings still key on queue pressure, not the honest utilization metric
detail: Briefing: "Warnings (amber 70 / red 90) ride the honest metric." The sim pipe-warning predicate (map telegraph, Pipe_Congested events) still rides queue pressure vs lane bound; only the NOC rail/overlay tints ride honest util. Warning events fold into the T1 hash, so changing this would move sim-truth goldens — the tension is documented in the artifact.
recommended_fix: None required if the ruling stands; record that the map telegraph is a queue-depth signal by design while rail amber/red ride utilization.
